result.rationale: In embeddable-host.js.es6 the delete action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', ...); }) with no .catch, whereas the save action in the same file uses .catch(popupAjaxError). A failed DELETE therefore produces an unhandled rejection and the row silently stays in the table with no user-visible error — the described mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the delete action (lines 42-48 of embeddable-host.js.es6), the destroyRecord() promise has no .catch() handler, unlike the save() action which uses .catch(popupAjaxError). If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the user receives no feedback about the failure. This is a real defect - inconsistent error handling where save shows errors but delete silently fails.
